questions.question: The current algorithm for intestinal parasites includes direct smears plus a concentration step and then an iron-hematoxylin (permanent trichrome-type) stain.
questions.question_raw: Current algorithm for intestinal parasites includes direct smears as well as concentrate and then iron hematoxylin stain.

parts.text: Name 4 clinically significant intestinal parasites that can be missed by this algorithm and 1 stain for each that you would use to detect them.

parts_raw.text: Name 4 clinically significant intestinal parasites that can be missed by this algorithm and 1 stain for each that you would use for them.

questions.model_answer: a) The routine ova-and-parasite algorithm (direct smear + formalin-ethyl-acetate concentration + iron-hematoxylin/trichrome permanent stain) does not reliably detect the intestinal coccidia or microsporidia, because their oocysts/spores stain poorly with iodine or trichrome and resemble yeast. Four missed pathogens and a dedicated stain for each: (1) Cryptosporidium spp. - modified acid-fast stain (modified Ziehl-Neelsen or Kinyoun; oocysts stain pink/red on a green-blue background), or auramine-rhodamine fluorescent stain / direct immunofluorescence. (2) Cyclospora cayetanensis - modified acid-fast stain (variably acid-fast; also autofluoresces under UV). (3) Cystoisospora (Isospora) belli - modified acid-fast stain. (4) Microsporidia (e.g., Enterocytozoon bieneusi, Encephalitozoon intestinalis) - modified trichrome stain (chromotrope 2R / Weber stain) or calcofluor white.
questions.beyond_mandell: Cyclospora, Cystoisospora and the microsporidian-specific stains (chromotrope 2R / calcofluor white) are established diagnostic practice (CDC DPDx; Mandell parasite-diagnosis chapters) rather than detailed in this Cryptosporidium chapter, which names acid-fast staining for Cryptosporidium and notes acid-fast stains also detect Cystoisospora and Cyclospora.
